note: Design briefs (each with a correct need, a decoy that hides the FIX inside the need, and a decoy that is too vague, all the same shape), constraints and society items for Technology And Society. ONE source: the game HTML gets this injected by build/technology-and-society-game.py, and the worksheet reads it. All examples are global. Checked by build/check-technology-and-society-game.py.

constraints.cheap: It must be made from things you could find at home, so it costs almost nothing.
constraints.noelec: It must work without electricity or batteries.
constraints.recycled: It must be made mostly from recycled materials.
constraints.pocket: It must be small enough to fit in a school bag.
constraints.rain: It must still work when it is wet.
constraints.child: A young child must be able to use it.

briefs.user: A farmer in a dry region
briefs.need: know when the crops need water
briefs.reason: watering too early or too late wastes water and harms the crop
briefs.measure: how many of 10 dry-soil tests it warns about correctly
briefs.solutionNeed: a soil sensor that beeps when the crops are dry
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to farm better when water is short

briefs.user: A student with a heavy school bag
briefs.need: carry books to school without hurting their back
briefs.reason: a heavy bag strains the back and shoulders
briefs.measure: how tired the carrier feels, from 1 to 5, after a 100 m walk
briefs.solutionNeed: a school bag with wheels and a long handle
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to make the school day much easier

briefs.user: An older person who forgets their medicine
briefs.need: remember to take medicine at the right time
briefs.reason: missing doses can stop the medicine working properly
briefs.measure: how many of 10 doses are taken at the right time
briefs.solutionNeed: a simple pill box with a loud alarm
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to look after their health at home

briefs.user: A family in a village with no mains electricity
briefs.need: light a room in the evening
briefs.reason: children cannot read or do homework when it is dark
briefs.measure: how many minutes the light lasts after a day outside
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to make evenings easier for the family

briefs.user: A cyclist who rides at night
briefs.need: be seen by drivers in the dark
briefs.reason: drivers who cannot see a cyclist may not stop in time
briefs.measure: the distance, in metres, at which a driver can see the cyclist
briefs.solutionNeed: a simple jacket with bright reflective strips
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to ride more safely on the roads

briefs.user: A nurse carrying vaccines on a long journey
briefs.reason: vaccines stop working if they get too warm
briefs.measure: how many hours the inside stays below 8 °C
briefs.solutionNeed: a cool box with ice packs

briefs.user: A school canteen that throws away a lot of food
briefs.reason: wasted food costs money and growing it harms the environment
briefs.measure: the mass of food thrown away each day, in kg
briefs.solutionNeed: a compost bin beside the canteen bins
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to run the canteen in a better way

briefs.user: A family whose home gets very hot in summer
briefs.reason: a hot room is uncomfortable and makes it hard to sleep or study
briefs.measure: the room temperature at 3 pm, in °C
briefs.solutionNeed: an air conditioner in every room
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to feel more comfortable at home

briefs.reason: needing help to open a door takes away independence
briefs.measure: the force needed to open the door, in newtons
briefs.solutionNeed: an automatic opener on every door
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to get around buildings more easily

briefs.need: carry water without holding a bottle
briefs.reason: holding a bottle tires the arm and spoils the running
briefs.measure: how far the bottle moves while running, in cm
briefs.solutionNeed: a waist belt that holds a water bottle
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to run more comfortably in races

briefs.user: A community whose river water is dirty
briefs.reason: dirty water can carry germs that make people ill
briefs.measure: how clear the water is, on a scale from 1 to 5
briefs.solutionNeed: a sand and charcoal filter by the river
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to improve the river

briefs.user: A resident of a town with a flooded street
briefs.reason: deep or fast water can knock people over and hide hazards
briefs.measure: how many of 10 people cross without slipping
briefs.solutionNeed: a raised walkway built over the street
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to cope with the flooding in town

briefs.user: A teacher in a noisy hall
briefs.need: be heard at the back of the room
briefs.reason: students who cannot hear cannot learn
briefs.measure: how many students at the back repeat a sentence correctly, out of 10
briefs.vagueNeed: a way to teach more effectively in the hall

society.text: People wanted to talk while away from home, so companies developed mobile phones.
A new law banned the gases that damage the ozone layer, so fridge makers changed the gas inside fridges.
Laws and safety campaigns pushed car makers to add seat belts and air bags.
Mobile phones let people read the news and send money from almost anywhere.
Fridges let families keep food fresh, so people began to shop less often.
The printing press made books cheaper, so more people could learn to read.
Fridges changed how families shop. Later a law changed the gas inside them.
Mobile phones changed how people bank. Governments then wrote new rules for mobile banking.
